newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:

World Bank President James Wolfensohn has proposed spending as much as $400 million over the next two years to restructure the lending institution and improve its performance in promoting the economic development of poor nations.

Prudential Insurance Co of America agreed to pay $19.4 million to Florida, Texas and Massachusettes to win their support for a $410 million class action settlement for charges that the company used deceptive sales practices.
NBC is presenting "Schindler's List" without commercial interruptions on Sunday night, thanks to an unusual offer from Ford Motor to sponsor the showing of the three-and-a-half hour film.
The Dow industrials fell 92.75 points to 6,927.38 on Thursday. The dollar fell and the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond rose to 6.65 percent from 6.57.
The death of paramount Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping raises questions over the pace of China's future economic reforms.
CompuServe reported a smaller-than-expected third quarter loss of $14.2 million, or $0.15 a share.

Ailing computer software company Borland International said it would lay off 300 people, or about 30 percent of its employees, at an estimated cost of $24 million to $30 million in the current quarter.
Initial claims for unemployment benefits rose less than expected last week, and construction starts on homes and apartments rose two percent.
Tandy reported stronger-than-expected fourth quarter results, posting operating earnings of $1.01 a share but a net loss of $2.39 a share.

The Transportation Safety Board determined that the Boeing 737 is less safe than other airlines because the failure of a valve controlling the rudder can cause a crash, but the board did not ground the aircrafts or declare them unsafe.
J.C. Penney's fourth quarter operating earnings fell despite a 23 percent rise in sales.
President Bill Clinton has moved to prohibit health maintenance organisations from limiting what doctors tell Medicaid patients about treatment options.
Soybean prices rose to five-month highs as delays to Brazil's harvest fuelled concerns that inventory levels could fall before the next American harvest.
A research scholar says corporate leaders who the first-born in their families are less innovative and adventurous than corporate heads who were born later in their families.
